findings.title: RDS instance without enhanced monitoring
findings.description: Hygiene: RDS instances should enable enhanced monitoring (monitoring_interval > 0) for OS-level metrics that aid troubleshooting. Set monitoring_interval to 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: RDS instance without enhanced monitoring
findings.description: monitoring_interval is absent or 0, so enhanced monitoring is disabled: OS-level metrics that catch host problems are missing. Set monitoring_interval between 1 and 60 seconds.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: RDS instance on the default option group
findings.description: option_group_name is absent or a default group, so the instance runs with AWS's generic options (e.g. no OEM, no MariaDB audit plugin). Use a purpose-built option group.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
